header.title: The Ultimate RYM Sampler Dashboard
header.author: Fouriels
header.meta.sources: Sources: Rate Your Music, Spotify, MusicBrainz, Discogs, Wikidata
footer.note: Album choices are each genre's highest-ranked RYM chart album that no other genre had already claimed (80% are the genre's #1) - the rest are typically in the top 5. 'Release year' means composition year for classical/traditional repertoire predating recording, and recording year otherwise. Artist origin comes from MusicBrainz, cited sources, and labeled inferences; track length comes from Spotify/MusicBrainz. Coverage gaps are documented above. Not affiliated with or endorsed by RateYourMusic or Sonemic.

popularity.title: Genre popularity, by release count
popularity.caveat: Every genre is one dot, on a log scale, shaded by how deep it sits in RYM's genre tree. A genre's count includes the releases of each of its subgenres (e.g Rock's count of {biggest} includes Alternative Rock's). A release tagged with several genres counts under each.
popularity.hint: Hover over a dot to see the genre; click it (or press Enter) for the artist, album, and track chosen for it. The arrow keys can be used to move up the genre list by number of releases.
popularity.tile.median.label: Median genre
popularity.tile.largest.label: Largest single genre
popularity.tile.under100.label: Genres with fewer than 100 releases
popularity.tile.over100k.label: Genres with 100,000 or more releases
treemap.title: RYM's top-level genres
treemap.caveat: Each rectangle is one of RYM's {n} top-level genres, sized by the release count of all of its subgenres. {a}, {b} and {c} alone account for {share} of all releases. Nb: releases can be counted twice if an album is counted as two genres (e.g Abbey Road is described as Pop Rock, and is counted as both Pop and Rock).
treemap.hint: Tap a genre to see its subgenres and representative albums.
decades.title: When each genre's top record came out
decades.caveat: For classical and traditional repertoire the year assigned is when the work was composed, not recorded. {n} genres ({share}) are modern recordings with no dateable release (e.g Australian Folk Music), and are marked Unknown.
decades.hint: Click a column to list the genres and representative albums from that decade.
heatmap.title: Where each family's records cluster in time
heatmap.caveat: A stronger colour = more top records of that genre fall in that decade.
heatmap.hint: Click a cell to list its genres, or click a family or decade label to list everything in that row or column.
heatmap.scaleCaption: genres in that family and decade
map.title: Where each genre's top record comes from
map.caveat: One album represents each genre (the #1 rated for {rank1} of them).
map.hint: Click a country on the map, or in the ranking, to list its artists and genres.
map.tile.top.label: Genres whose top record is by an artist from {country}
map.tile.top.note: {n} of the {known} genres with a known country
map.tile.second.label: …and from {country}, the runner-up
map.tile.known.label: Genres with a known artist country
map.fineprint.summary: How each artist's country was found, and how far to trust it
map.fineprint.origin: Artist origin is resolved for {n} of {total} genres ({share}) across {codes} country or area codes, using MusicBrainz, Wikidata and cited artist sources.
map.fineprint.agreement: {n} are inferred where a country-specific RYM genre and the earliest matching release country agree.
map.fineprint.discogs: {n} are read from a single unambiguous "from <country>" sentence in the artist's own Discogs profile (about 85% agreement with MusicBrainz when checked; a same-named act can occasionally be matched).
map.fineprint.implied: {n} more are inferred from the genre's own name alone (e.g. "Cretan Folk Music" → Greece) - when the same rule was replayed on artists whose country is independently known it agreed about 85% of the time, so treat those as likely rather than confirmed.
map.fineprint.territories: Small territories and non-country areas may appear in the table without a shape on the map.
duration.title: How long is a genre's top track?
duration.caveat: The most popular track on each genre's top-rated album, one dot per genre, shaded by the genre's level in RYM's tree. The median song length is between {lo} and {hi} at every genre depth.
duration.hint: Hover a dot to name the genre and its length; click it (or press Enter) for the artist, album and track. The arrow keys can be used to increase or decrease by length.
duration.axisTitle: length of the genre's top track (minutes)
duration.tile.median.label: Median track
duration.tile.under3.label: Shorter than 3 minutes
duration.tile.over10.label: 10 minutes or longer
regional.title: Regional Music is a strange 'genre'
regional.caveat: 'Regional Music' is a fairly ill-defined genre family which mostly encompasses non-Western music, although not exclusively. At times it can be quite arbitrary - Hiplife (Ghanaian Hip Hop) counts as 'regional', but Memphis Rap doesn't.
regional.hint: Click a region to list its genres.
regional.tile.home.label: Genres that count as 'Regional Music' only
regional.tile.under.label: Genres somewhere under Regional Music
overlap.title: Half of the genres have two homes
overlap.caveat: {n} genres ({share}) belong to more than one genre family.
overlap.hint: Click a pair to list the genres that belong to both.
depth.title: How deep the tree goes
depth.hint: Click a column to list the genres at that depth.
artists.title: Artists sampled more than once
artists.caveat: There are {n} distinct artists across {total} genres - and most appear exactly once - but some crop up multiple times.
artists.hint: Click an artist to list their associated genres.
scripts.title: Writing systems in the names
scripts.caveat: {n} non-Latin scripts appear across artist/track/album names (the Latin alphabet itself appears in 2,608 of 2,613, and is excluded here to keep the chart legible).
scripts.hint: Click a writing system to list the genres whose artist, track, or album name uses it.
obscurity.title: How obscure is the #1 pick?
obscurity.caveat: Spotify's own 0–100 popularity score, known for {share} of genres (the tracks with a matched Spotify id). 0 means Spotify has almost no play signal for it at all.
obscurity.hint: Click a column to list the tracks with that Spotify score.
hero.footer: Every Genre on RateYourMusic, by the numbers
hero.regional.title: More than half of all genres sit under Regional Music. Only a quarter call it home.
hero.regional.sub: Each dot is one genre. The taxonomy is a graph, not a tree: a genre can belong to several families, and Regional Music is the one that reaches into most of them.
hero.regional.source: Source: RateYourMusic genre taxonomy, chart snapshot April 2026. “Calls it home” = the family reached by the shortest ancestry path; every genre is counted once.
hero.regional.stat.shared: {n} more sit under it as one of several homes — mostly Folk ({a}) and {b} ({c}).
hero.regional.note: Counted by every membership, Regional Music reaches {under} of {total} genres. Counted by home — one family per genre — it is {home}. The gap is genres that are Folk, Classical or Pop first, and regional second.
hero.map.title: The top record in one genre in four is by an American artist.
hero.map.sub: Each of RateYourMusic’s {genres} genres is represented by its top-rated album. Where that album’s artist comes from is known for {known} genres, across {codes} countries and areas — and {us}% of those are American.
hero.map.source: Source: RateYourMusic chart snapshot, April 2026: one album per genre — its #1, or the best one no other genre had claimed. Artist origin: MusicBrainz, Wikidata and cited artist sources; {unknown} genres have no single-country answer and are not shown.
hero.map.note: This counts genres, not releases, and RYM’s taxonomy leans Western. Coverage is uneven too: an artist country is known for {eu}% of European Music genres but {af}% of African Music ones — so a pale country can mean sparser data, not less music.
hero.popularity.title: {rock} has nearly a million charted releases. The median genre has {median}.
hero.popularity.sub: Releases per genre, on a log scale — each dot is one genre, shaded by how deep it sits in RYM’s genre tree. {under100} genres ({share}) have fewer than 100.
hero.popularity.source: Source: RateYourMusic chart snapshot, April 2026. A genre’s count includes its subgenres’ releases (part of why top-level genres sit furthest right), and a release tagged with several genres counts under each.
hero.popularity.keyIntro: Shade = level in the tree, with each level’s median:
hero.popularity.medianNote: Half of all genres have fewer than this.
hero.treemap.title: {a}, {b} and {c} hold {share} of the releases on RateYourMusic.
hero.treemap.sub: Each rectangle is one of RYM’s {n} top-level genres, sized by the number of charted releases filed under it and everything beneath it — {total} in all. Colour follows size.
hero.treemap.source: Source: RateYourMusic chart snapshot, April 2026. Each top-level genre’s count already includes its subgenres’. A release filed under several genres counts under each (Abbey Road is both Pop and Rock), so these are filings, not distinct albums.
hero.treemap.note: Outlined: the three biggest. “Uncategorised” gathers the {u} genres RYM files under no top-level genre.
hero.treemap.small: Too small to label, largest first: {names}.
hero.decades.title: Six years into the 2020s, more genres have their top record from it than from the 1970s.
hero.decades.sub: Each bar counts the genres whose top-rated record came out in that decade. {unknown} more genres ({unknownShare}) are modern traditions with no dateable release, and are not shown.
hero.decades.source: Source: RateYourMusic chart snapshot, April 2026; release years from Discogs, MusicBrainz, Spotify and RYM. Classical and traditional repertoire is dated by when the work was composed, not recorded. “Before 1900” includes {ancient} ancient and medieval traditions with no single year.
hero.decades.callout: {n20} genres have their top record from the 2020s — a decade that is only six years old. The 1970s have {n70}; the 1980s, {n80}.
hero.heatmap.title: Every genre family has its decade. Line them up and they march through time.
hero.heatmap.sub: Each row is one of RYM’s {families} genre families; a cell is how many of its genres have their top record from that decade, relative to the family’s own busiest decade (outlined). Sorted by that peak: Blues in the 1960s, Rock in the 1970s, Metal in the 1990s, Hip Hop in the 2020s.
hero.heatmap.source: Source: RateYourMusic chart snapshot, April 2026; release years as for the decades chart. n = the family’s genres with a dateable top record. Small families are noisy: {small} each have fewer than ten. Classical Music is dated by when works were composed.
hero.duration.title: The top track of the typical genre lasts {median}. The longest lasts {longest}.
hero.duration.sub: Each dot is one genre, stacked by the length of the most popular track on its top-rated album and shaded by its level in RYM’s genre tree. The median barely moves with depth: {lo} to {hi} at every level.
hero.duration.source: Source: RateYourMusic chart snapshot, April 2026; track lengths from Spotify and MusicBrainz, known for {n} of {genres} genres ({share}). Past 12 minutes the columns widen: 12–15, 15–20, 20–30, 30–60 minutes, and over an hour.
